title: K-injective quotient-projection comparison on arbitrary shifted replacements
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R$ and uniformizer $t$, and a finite-type $k$-scheme $W$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. On a fixed small skeleton $\mathcal V=W_{\mathrm{proet}}$ set $B_n=(R/t^n)_W$ for $n\ge1$ and $A=\lim_nB_n$. Let $\mathcal T$ be the ringed sequence site with ring $B=(B_n)_n$, and let $\mathscr S_W=\operatorname{Mod}_{\mathcal T}(B)$ be its strict quotient-semilinear module systems [def-coef-ringed-sequence-site]. Use ordinary unbounded derived categories and cochain shifts, with $d_{K[r]}=(-1)^r d_K$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Fix a supplied coefficient calculus $S$ with its coherence data, reduction $\mathcal R$ and total limit $\mathcal L=R\lim D(U)$ [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]; $U$ is termwise scalar restriction along $A\to B_n$.

Let $p:(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal T),B)\to(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal V),A)$ be the ringed projection whose underlying inverse image is the constant-system functor $c$ and whose structural map $cA\to B$ consists of the quotient projections [def-pur-ringed-topos-morphism-of-universes].

Factor $p=g\circ a$ through the constant ring $cA$ on $\mathcal T$, so $a_*=U$ is exact and $g_*=\lim$. There is a canonical natural isomorphism
$$\kappa:Rp_*\xrightarrow{\sim}Rg_*D(U)=\mathcal L.$$
Its normalization on every K-injective $B$-system complex $I$ [def-pur-kinjective-complex] and any K-injective replacement $j:UI\to J$ over $cA$ is the quasi-isomorphism $\lim j:\lim UI\to\lim J$ representing $\kappa_{[I]}$ under the canonical resolution identifications [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition]. Here $[K]$ denotes the derived object of a complex $K$.

For every strict $B$-system complex $N$ and every simultaneous K-injective replacement $v:UN\to J$, there is a canonical isomorphism $\mathcal L([N])\xrightarrow{\sim}[\lim J]$. It is the localization comparison followed by $R\lim([v])$ and the canonical K-injective model comparison. For any K-injective replacement $i:N\to I$ over $B$, there is a unique homotopy class $b:UI\to J$ with $bUi\simeq v$; $b$ is a quasi-isomorphism, and $\lim b$ represents the composite $Rp_*[N]\xrightarrow{\kappa}\mathcal L([N])\xrightarrow{\sim}[\lim J]$ in the model $Rp_*[N]=[\lim UI]$. These identifications are independent of $i$, natural for arbitrary derived morphisms in $N$, and satisfy the change-of-resolution cocycle formulas.

For every $r\in\mathbf Z$, the replacement for $I[r]$ is exactly $j[r]$, and the comparison is $\lim(j[r])=(\lim j)[r]$ under $\lim(J[r])=(\lim J)[r]$, with degree-$i$ map $\lim j^{i+r}$. For a supplied $v$ the shifted replacement is exactly $v[r]$, with comparison class $b[r]$. These equations hold naturally for all derived inputs and maps and respect shift zero, addition and inverse shifts. No preservation of K-injectives by $U$, exactness of arbitrary products, boundedness or normalized-system hypothesis is assumed.

proof.text: Identify the actual coefficient restriction functor with sequence-to-strict-system equivalence followed by the sectionwise restrictionFunctor of lem-coef-restricted-tower-resolution-acyclicity. The identification uses uniqueness of coefficientSequenceRestriction: the vertical coefficient maps are both the identity on sections, and horizontal and morphism maps are the original section maps. The equivalence is additive and preserves K-injective complexes. Apply the existing restricted-tower acyclicity theorem to the identity resolution of the transported K-injective system. Transport back along the complex comparison isomorphism to obtain that lim j is a quasi-isomorphism for every supplied j:UI→J with I,J K-injective.

Use the canonical total inverse limit after exact restriction itself as RP. Its unit on complexes is η_UI followed by Rlim of the inverse exact-localization comparison. Naturality of the derived unit and exact-localization comparison proves this is a natural transformation. The K-injective model unit is inverse to the existing rightDerivedFunctorObjQIso. Consequently the unit followed by the supplied replacementIso(v) is exactly [lim v]. Enough K-injective resolutions on the actual ringed sequence site and the preceding acyclicity show the unit invertible on every K-injective system. The K-injective derivability structure, via CategoryTheory.derives, makes this unit a right derived functor. Set κ to the identity isomorphism; right-derived uniqueness proves uniqueness from its normalization on every complex. For efficient specialization, define the general comparison and the same normalization, arbitrary-replacement, naturality, cocycle, and shift predicates for an exact additive F followed by additive G. The coefficient predicates specialize these formulas to U and lim; their quantifiers and equations are definitionally unchanged. All general calculations are proved privately in this module before specialization.

For supplied i:N→I and v:UN→J, use the Mathlib homotopy-to-derived Hom bijection into the K-injective J to lift [Ui]⁻¹[v] to a homotopy class b. The same injectivity makes precomposition by Ui injective and gives the specified iff characterization of b. Every chain representative β satisfies Ui β homotopic to v; localization and cancellation imply β is a quasi-isomorphism. The first step gives that lim β is a quasi-isomorphism. Naturality of the canonical unit and exact-localization comparison proves the displayed arbitrary-replacement formula.

Postcompose replacementIso(v) by the invertible derived unit at J. It becomes Rlim of the exact-localization comparison followed by [v]. Thus the given equation for a derived morphism f and a comparison s proves the replacementIso naturality square by cancellation. Apply exact restriction to the equation represented by t and use the two supplied comparison homotopies to obtain equality of the classes of βs and Utβ′. The K-injective Hom injectivity gives the required homotopy. For three replacements, cancel the localized initial quasi-isomorphism to obtain composition and identity equations; Hom injectivity gives their homotopies, and additive inverse limit sends these homotopies to the displayed derived equations. The same argument with additive push proves the system-resolution cocycle.

Use Mathlib closure of K-injectives and quasi-isomorphisms under cochain shifts. Termwise inverse limit has the asserted components by definition, and additivity gives its differential sign. Shift the supplied comparison homotopy and precompose with the standard restriction shift isomorphism; its naturality gives the stated shifted comparison. Use the proved canonical-unit shift helper of lem-sp-canonical-right-derived-adjunction-shift: first restrict to the K-injective subcategory of the homotopy category. Its expression through the K-injective equivalence and its counit commutes with shifts by the construction of rightDerivedFunctor.CommShift. Every complex admits a quasi-isomorphism to a K-injective, so cancel its invertible image to descend unit shift compatibility. Whiskering and composing with exact-localization shift compatibility gives the unit compatibility for RP. Finally postcompose the desired replacement shift equation by the shifted invertible unit at J; unit shift compatibility, naturality of the derived shift isomorphisms, and exact-localization shift compatibility reduce both sides to the same composite. This proves the prescribed shifts using the canonical coherent Mathlib commutation structures.
